pav_guide.text: The Banqueting Room. Look up: a silver dragon holding a chandelier that weighs nearly a ton. The Prince's guests ate dinners of a hundred dishes under it.
The kitchen's through there, with cast-iron columns made to look like palm trees. Nash used iron to hold up the domes too. All this fantasy, built with the latest engineering.
George loved this place. When he became king, he hardly came back. Too busy, then too big; he'd eaten too many of those dinners.

pav_cook.text: The great chef Antonin Careme cooked here in 1817. One famous banquet had over a hundred dishes, from soups to towering sugar sculptures.
Careme only stayed a few months. He said the English weather didn't suit him. The weather says the same about everybody.
